title: Ezekiel Chapter 30 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 30 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 30 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 30.

questions.question: What did the word of the LORD come to Ezekiel saying?
options: Repent, for the kingdom is near.
Fear not, for I am with you.
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel saying, 'Thus saith the Lord GOD; Howl ye, Woe worth the day!' (Ezekiel 30:2).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30, what will come upon Egypt?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And the sword shall come upon Egypt...' (Ezekiel 30:4).

questions.question: Which nations are mentioned as falling by the sword?
questions.explanation: The verse lists these nations: 'Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mingled people, and Chub...' (Ezekiel 30:5).

questions.question: True or False: The pride of Egypt's power shall come down according to Ezekiel 30.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the pride of her power shall come down...' (Ezekiel 30:6).

questions.question: What shall happen to the cities of Egypt according to Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: The chapter says, 'they shall be desolate in the midst of the countries that are desolate...' (Ezekiel 30:7).

questions.question: True or False: Messengers will go forth from the Lord in ships to comfort the Ethiopians.
questions.explanation: The messengers will make the careless Ethiopians afraid, not comfort them (Ezekiel 30:9).

questions.question: Who will make the multitude of Egypt to cease?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I will also make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.' (Ezekiel 30:10).

questions.question: True or False: The rivers of Egypt will be made dry according to Ezekiel 30.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I will make the rivers dry...' (Ezekiel 30:12).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 30, what will happen to the idols in Egypt?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I will also destroy the idols...' (Ezekiel 30:13).

questions.question: What city will have a fire set in it according to Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'I will set fire in Zoan...' (Ezekiel 30:14).

questions.question: True or False: The young men of Aven and of Pibeseth shall fall by the sword.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The young men of Aven and of Pibeseth shall fall by the sword...' (Ezekiel 30:17).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 30, which event occurs FIRST?
options: The young men of Aven fall by the sword
questions.explanation: The sword coming upon Egypt is mentioned as an early event in the chapter (Ezekiel 30:4).

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 30 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 30 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the multitude of Egypt according to Ezekiel 30:10?
options: It will cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
It will become allies with Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: It will cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:10 clearly states that the multitude of Egypt will cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar, indicating a complete downfall of Egypt's power.

questions.question: Who will be brought to destroy the land of Egypt according to Ezekiel 30:11?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:11 mentions that Nebuchadrezzar and his people, described as 'the terrible of the nations', will come to destroy Egypt.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30:12, what will happen to the rivers in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:12 states that the LORD will make the rivers dry, indicating a significant judgment against the land.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:13 say will happen to the idols in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:13 declares that the LORD will destroy the idols and cease their images, showcasing His power over false gods.

questions.question: What biblical truth can we gather from Ezekiel 30:14 regarding judgment?
options: Judgment is only for foreign nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:14 shows that God executes judgments on Egypt, emphasizing that disobedience leads to unavoidable consequences.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30:15, what will happen to Sin, the strength of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:15 states that Sin shall have great pain, indicating the severe judgment that is to come upon Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 30:19 states that the Egyptians will know the LORD after His judgments.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:19 confirms that through the execution of judgments, the Egyptians shall know that He is the LORD.

questions.question: What will happen to the young men of Aven and Pibeseth according to Ezekiel 30:17?
options: They will be taken as captives
They will fall by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They will fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:17 states that the young men of Aven and Pibeseth shall fall by the sword, indicating the violence that will come.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 30:21 says that the arm of Pharaoh shall be healed.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:21 clearly states that the arm of Pharaoh will not be bound up to be healed, indicating a permanent defeat.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:25 indicate about Pharaoh's arms?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:25 states that Pharaoh's arms shall fall down, signifying his loss of power in the face of judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 30:24 illustrate God's sovereignty over nations?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 30:24, God declares that He will strengthen the arms of Nebuchadrezzar, showing His control over the rise and fall of nations.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Ezekiel 30:12 regarding integrity in leadership?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:12 illustrates that the land will be made waste due to the wickedness of its leaders, teaching that integrity is crucial.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 30:22 indicates that God is in favor of Pharaoh's reign.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:22 shows that God is against Pharaoh, indicating opposition to his authority and reign.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 30 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 30.

questions.question: What proclamation does the Lord make regarding the day of the Lord in Ezekiel 30?
options: It shall be a day of rejoicing
It shall be a cloudy day
It shall be a day of peace
It shall be a day of prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be a cloudy day
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:3 states that 'For the day is near, even the day of the LORD is near, a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen.'

questions.question: Who will the sword come upon according to Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:4 mentions, 'And the sword shall come upon Egypt...' indicating that Egypt is the target of divine judgment.

questions.question: What will happen to the pride of Egypt's power according to Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:6 declares, '...the pride of her power shall come down...' indicating the downfall of Egypt's strength.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30:10, who will cause the multitude of Egypt to cease?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:10 states, 'I will also make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.'

questions.question: What does the Lord say He will do to the idols of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:13 states, 'I will also destroy the idols, and I will cause their images to cease out of Noph...' showing God's intent to eliminate false worship.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 30, the young men of which cities shall fall by the sword?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:17 states, 'The young men of Aven and of Pibeseth shall fall by the sword...' indicating judgment on these locations.

questions.question: What does the Lord say He has done to Pharaoh's arm?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:21 states, 'Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt...' indicating divine judgment against Pharaoh.

questions.question: What will happen to the Egyptians according to Ezekiel 30:23?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:23 states, 'And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations...' indicating their dispersion as a form of punishment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30:25, who will have their arms strengthened?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:24 states, 'And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon...' illustrating God's support for Babylon against Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: The Egyptians will know that the Lord is God after the judgments are executed.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:19 states, 'Thus will I execute judgments in Egypt: and they shall know that I am the LORD.' confirming that they will recognize God's sovereignty.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord states that He is against Pharaoh king of Egypt.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:22 declares, 'Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt...' indicating God's opposition to Pharaoh.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the structure of Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: The chapter features a chiasm where themes of judgment and divine intervention are mirrored, focusing on Egypt's downfall and Babylon's rise.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage connects to the theme of God's judgment on Egypt as seen in Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:25-26 echoes themes of judgment against Egypt, resonating with the proclamations found in Ezekiel 30.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage reinforces the idea of scattering as a consequence of sin similar to Ezekiel 30?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28:64 mentions God scattering His people among the nations as a consequence of disobedience, akin to the scattering of Egyptians in Ezekiel 30.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 30 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 30 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:2 indicate about the tone of the prophecy regarding Egypt?
options: It is a message of hope
It is a warning of destruction
It is a call to repentance
It is a celebration of victory
questions.correctAnswer: It is a warning of destruction
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:2 states 'Thus saith the Lord GOD; Howl ye, Woe worth the day!' indicating a tone of lamentation and warning about impending destruction.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 30:4, which nations are mentioned as being affected by the sword?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:4 mentions, 'the sword shall come upon Egypt, and great pain shall be in Ethiopia,' directly indicating the nations affected.

questions.question: What will happen to the pride of Egypt according to Ezekiel 30:6?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:6 states, 'the pride of her power shall come down,' indicating a loss of strength and arrogance.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:8 reveal about God's purpose in the destruction of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:8 indicates that 'they shall know that I am the LORD,' signifying that the destruction is meant to reveal God's sovereignty and power.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30:10, who will bring an end to the multitude of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:10 states, 'I will also make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon,' clearly identifying the agent of destruction.

questions.question: What does God's action of drying up rivers symbolize in Ezekiel 30:12?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:12 indicates that 'I will make the rivers dry... and make the land waste,' symbolizing God's judgment and desolation upon Egypt.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 30:13, what specific action does God say He will take regarding idols in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:13 states, 'I will also destroy the idols,' indicating a direct action against the false gods of Egypt.

questions.question: What is indicated about the fate of the cities in Ezekiel 30:15?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:15 mentions, 'Sin shall have great pain, and No shall be rent asunder,' indicating destruction and devastation.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:19 suggest about the overall purpose of God's judgments in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:19 states, 'Thus will I execute judgments in Egypt,' emphasizing God's role as a just judge.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:21 signify about Pharaoh's condition?
options: His arm will not be healed
questions.correctAnswer: His arm will not be healed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:21 indicates, 'lo, it shall not be bound up to be healed,' showing Pharaoh's incapacitation and weakness.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 30:24, what will happen to Pharaoh's arms?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:24 mentions, 'I will break Pharaoh's arms,' indicating a complete and definitive judgment against him.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 30:25 reveal about the relationship between God and the king of Babylon?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:25 states, 'I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon,' indicating God's support for Babylon against Egypt.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight do Ezekiel 30:6 and Ezekiel 30:12 provide regarding God's sovereignty over nations?
options: God allows nations to thrive without consequences
God actively judges nations for their actions
God has no control over earthly rulers
questions.correctAnswer: God actively judges nations for their actions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:6 and 30:12 demonstrate that God exercises sovereign control over nations, bringing judgment upon Egypt for its pride and sin.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ezekiel 30:20 and Ezekiel 30:26 convey about God's communication with His prophets?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:20 and 30:26 show that God speaks clearly to His prophets about His intentions, emphasizing His desire for His people to know His plans.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 30:4-5 reflect the theme of communal judgment in the context of nations?
options: Judgment is limited to one city
Multiple nations share in the judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Multiple nations share in the judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 30:4-5 highlights that not only Egypt but also Ethiopia, Libya, and others will fall, indicating a communal aspect of divine judgment.
